title: etw: support TraceLogging, include Extended Data, display individual properties, new capture settings
description:
This PR refactors the ETW dissector and collector

- adds support for non manifest-based events, like Windows 10's+ [TraceLogging](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/tracelogging/trace-logging-portal), which currently cannot be sniffed because etwdump doesn't try to call the formatter if it doesn't find a XML-like formatting message
- heavily rework wireshark's internal ETL wrapping (the "protocol" that only exists between etwdump and the wireshark dissector that includes the raw event + some elements formatted by asking the [Tdh](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/tdh/) api).
  - I have extended it to also retrieve the "[Extended Data](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/evntcons/ns-evntcons-event_header_extended_data_item)" and the properties without formatting. It contains the schema that's used for tracelogging, and optionally some extra information that can be enabled with flags when starting the capture (like the stacktrace, the SID of the process that did the event, etc.).
  - the formatting of the user message is now done in the parser (as opposed to within etwdump), which allows to see the unformatted properties and filter on them
  - the properties are now parsed separately
- add the ability to enable some capture flags in etwdump. The results will show up in one of the "Extended Data" items.
- show what kind of ETW logs is being captured in a note: manifest-based, MOF (classic / legacy), WPP or Tracelogging

New capture options :

![image](/uploads/a6d0c64c54dff798427246a818b4f52d/image.png){width=447 height=359}

The extended data blobs :

![image](/uploads/6e1a045894180e2e1c01e7c807482595/image.png){width=645 height=600}

Some formatting changes and improvements :

![image](/uploads/1b768e74ea7243634db6507b3bdd5893/image.png){width=788 height=336}

I have another PR that builds onto this one that brings improved support for some specific providers (currently Wireshark has a cases for 2 ETW providers: the "Network Interface Capture" and the "MBIM" providers). It's unfinished and the PR was becoming too big, so it will come later. It will be possible to display decrypted SMB and LDAP messages, and similar cool features that Microsoft Message Analyzer had, by tapping in the proper ETW traces.

(See also https://github.com/the-tcpdump-group/tcpdump-htdocs/pull/53 to have LINKTYPE_ETW updated. I'm unsure if it makes sense to have this standardized since it's basically a Wireshark-only internal, but it was already standardized)

AI-Assisted: no
